Confusable pairs among the restriction, endorsement and small-vehicle rules, followed by continuation facts the main list did not hold; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec03-R01 | anchor: A01
On the code chart, B as a license restriction means glasses or contact lenses, while B as an ID card endorsement means motor driven cycle. [A01]
Why it matters: group codes; confusable restriction B versus endorsement B.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec03-R02 | anchor: A01
Restriction G means daylight driving only, while restriction J on the license chart means specific limitations. [A01]
Why it matters: group codes; confusable G versus J.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec03-R03 | anchor: A01
Endorsement 2 on a base license means for-hire, while restriction 2 means HTV conditional. [A01]
Why it matters: group codes; confusable endorsement versus restriction number.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec03-R04 | anchor: A03
An autocycle needs only a valid driver's license, while an MDC can be ridden on an ID card that carries an MDC endorsement. [A03]
Why it matters: group small vehicles; confusable autocycle versus MDC credential.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-R05 | anchor: A03
Autocycle riders sit on a seat, but MDC riders must sit astride the seat with a leg on each side. [A03]
Why it matters: group small vehicles; confusable seating position.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-R06 | anchor: A03
Any MDC rider must be at least 15, but the helmet and eye-protection rules apply only to riders under 18. [A03]
Why it matters: group small vehicles; confusable minimum age versus gear age.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-R07 | anchor: A02
A license with a motorcycle endorsement can be renewed up to two years early. [A02]
Why it matters: group renewal windows; confusable with for-hire renewal window.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-R08 | anchor: A04
A license with a for-hire endorsement can be renewed only up to one year early. [A04]
Why it matters: group renewal windows; confusable with motorcycle renewal window.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-R09 | anchor: A02
A new resident with an out-of-state motorcycle credential takes the motorcycle knowledge exam only, with no riding skills exam. [A02]
Why it matters: group transfers; confusable new resident versus first-time rider.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-R10 | anchor: A04
A new resident aged 18 or older who already holds a for-hire endorsement from another state on a valid license, a chauffeur or public passenger chauffeur license, or a CDL adds the Indiana for-hire endorsement after passing the for-hire knowledge exam. [A04]
Why it matters: group transfers; scope note for-hire.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-R11 | anchor: A04
A for-hire bus is a bus that carries passengers for hire or is operated for compensation. [A04]
Why it matters: group for-hire; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-R12 | anchor: A04
Moving a recreational vehicle before its first retail sale is not for-hire transport when it weighs no more than 26,000 pounds, or when the combined weight with the towing vehicle is no more than 26,000 pounds and the towed unit is no more than 10,000 pounds. [A04]
Why it matters: group for-hire; difficulty high.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-R13 | anchor: A02
The BMV strongly encourages motorcycle safety courses from Ride Safe Indiana providers, listed at RideSafeIndiana.com. [A02]
Why it matters: group motorcycle; scope note motorcycle only.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-R14 | anchor: A01
A restricted license for a driver with disabilities can name the particular equipment the driver must use in the vehicle. [A01]
Why it matters: group special needs; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]
